review.summary: Review of the lab's genus >= 2 prime-field index-calculus work, current to 2026-11-20. Everything quoted from the repo is [pcc:unverified]: no result in this area has a replay certificate, VALIDATION.json or §5a-band matched rho. The genus-4 prime-order study is the one that went through a validator replay, with ERRATA (disposition 'validated'). Genus-4 results are still absent from docs/ic/LEADERBOARD.md and benchmarks/README.md. Bottom line: no lead has changed an exponent. The measured gains are constants: relation-phase cost (L01), linear algebra (SGE, base constant, Ferrari), and the Smith transfer at genus 3. Every comparison is on toy primes, and the three-phase cost is complete (relation, linear algebra, descent, setup) only for the genus-4 studies and the Smith transfer study. The only genus where the lab has IC below the strongest rho under a conservative price (w = 1 GAE per native op) is genus 4, and that rests on 2 primes (16411, 32771), 5 curves each. Genus 3 is below rho only at w = 0 or in FPM-mid units. Genus 2 is 3-5x above rho and flat, so there is no crossing. The orchestrator should know three things. (1) The lead atlas path /home/user/crypto-autoresearcher/knowledge/leads/ecdlp/ does not exist on this host, and research-kb was not queried, so all literature exponents below are recalled from repo docs (SUCCESS_CRITERIA.md, hec_ic_speedup PLAN.md, L08/L12 PROTOCOL) and are literature-unverified. (2) The 2026-11-15 to 2026-11-17 session logs are 70 MB, 2 MB and 7.6 MB, so I grepped headings rather than reading them. (3) F1, F2 and F3 (g2plus_followups_20261117) have frozen protocols and pilot gate-reachability only, with no decision run. Unexamined, so unreviewed: hec_* directories not named in the results below (about 150 in total), ghs_*, gaudry_quartic_*, binary-field studies (not prime-field), and the 'Lead D' transfer atlas (stopped by safeguards).

Assessor caveat: the naive route is not a lower bound for Prym IC; the Abel-Prym E-E^sigma family may give 2-2/g (equal to the hyperelliptic bar) at the cost of a non-linear fibre problem. Pricing band (AGENTS.md §5a): every cross-method comparison must price native work at w = 0, 0.1 and 1 GAE per native operation and rank two arms only where the order holds across the band. Almost every lab genus >= 2 row fails this: genus 3-5 are far below rho at w=0 and above or unresolved at w=1 (genus 5 p=1031: 0.0030, 0.090, 0.48 [0.27,1.14]; genus 3 unresolved at every prime). Rho reference choice moves ratios by 1.3-1.7x: for genus 4 the ideal negation bound sqrt(pi r/4) (charges nothing for canonicalisation or fruitless cycles) is 1.41x tighter than expected plain rho sqrt(pi r/2); at genus 4 plain rho costs 1.30x negation rho in the lab's walk (window/Brent compares ~18 per step unpriced in an earlier band). proposals.title: Decide the affine-type (2,2,2) codomain type: the single gate for a UNIVERSAL genus-3 prime-order exponent drop 4/3 -> 1
proposals.mechanism: Every prime-order (odd-degree-model) genus-3 hyperelliptic Jacobian J/F_q has exactly two F_q-rational (2,2,2)-kernels, both AFFINE-type (the extended-Hamming/AGL_3(F_2) Lagrangians of J[2]); I verified this by exact enumeration (0 rational pair-type, 2 rational affine-type). Because #J is PRIME, J is F_q-simple, so the quotient J/L is a SIMPLE dim-3 ppav = a Jacobian of a smooth genus-3 curve, which is EITHER hyperelliptic OR a plane quartic (decomposable is impossible). If it is a plane quartic, apply Diem's plane-curve index calculus O~(q) and recover the DL, transferring exponent 4/3 -> 1. The kernel points sit over F_{q^7} (Frobenius acts as a single 7-cycle on the 7 nonzero kernel points), a CONSTANT-degree extension, and the (2,2,2)-theta isogeny (Lubicz-Robert) is poly(2^3)=O(1) theta operations plus a level-4 theta structure over a further bounded (q-independent) extension, so the whole transfer is poly(log q) -- negligible beside q. Decisive binary question: is that codomain a quartic or hyperelliptic?
proposals.applies_to: Genus-3 hyperelliptic curves, prime-order Jacobian, odd-degree (deg-7) model, over prime F_q. Coverage if the codomain is a quartic: ~100% of prime-order curves (two rational affine kernels ALWAYS exist). If it is hyperelliptic: 0% gain.
proposals.predicted_cost: Transfer/setup: poly(log q) = O~(1) in q (Frobenius charpoly factor + CRT idempotent for the kernel; kernel points over F_{q^7}; level-4 theta structure over a bounded extension; one (2,2,2) theta isogeny; codomain curve + Serre-twist descent; evaluate the isogeny on the 2 target divisors). Relation + linear algebra + descent on the quartic: Diem O~(q^1). End-to-end exponent 1, vs 2LP q^(4/3) and rho q^(3/2). Every phase charged; the only non-polylog phase is Diem's O~(q).
proposals.baseline_beaten: Hyperelliptic double-large-prime IC O~(q^4/3) (lab-measured genus-3 2LP exponent 1.344 [1.334,1.358], research/genus_ladder_scale_20261115/RESULTS.md per prior-work review [pcc:unverified]) and rho q^(3/2); exponents cited research/g2plus_leads_20261116/L06_odd_ell_isogeny_census/ASSESSMENT_RERUN.md sec 5 and docs/ic/SUCCESS_CRITERIA.md. ONLY beaten if the codomain is a quartic.
proposals.prior_work_check: Existence of exactly 2 rational affine (2,2,2)-kernels is in the lab (L06 DERIVATION.md lines 160-172) and I re-derived it; Smith's construction reaches the quartic ONLY from PAIR-type kernels (smith_canonical_20261115/PROTOCOL.md L15, RESULTS.md), which are structurally absent for prime order (smith_near_prime_20261114/RESULTS.md: k=1 irreducible f, 0 of 1110). The codomain type of the AFFINE-type quotient is explicitly UNDETERMINED in the lab (L06 DERIVATION sec 4 and sec 6; ASSESSMENT_RERUN sec 5 item 2 'the decisive question') and, per the lab, NOT checked against literature (research-kb was unavailable, L06 sec 7). Note: Smith's prime-order restriction is about RATIONALITY of his pairing-based construction, NOT about which quotients are quartics -- so the affine quotient may well be a quartic that Smith simply had no tool to compute. Determination = plausibly-new.
proposals.key_risk: The codomain is HYPERELLIPTIC (then zero exponent gain -- my honest prior is ~50/50, since Smith's 0% for prime order concerns his construction's rationality, not the quotient's type). Secondary: the level-4 theta structure forces a large (but q-independent) extension inflating the constant; evaluating the isogeny on divisors to carry the DL adds cost; Diem's O~(q) hides constants the lab has not validated for generic prime-order quartics (see Proposal 2).
proposals.cheapest_falsifying_test: The type is a GENERIC moduli property (all 30 affine Lagrangians are S_8-equivalent; one example settles it for ~all curves). Step 0 (hours): read Smith 2009 and Ritzenthaler's genus-3 theta criteria for the full 135-kernel classification -- it may already state the affine-quotient type. Step 1 (1-2 days): install a CAS (none on host) and compute ONE affine-type (2,2,2)-isogeny on ONE toy prime-order genus-3 curve over F_{q^7} with a genus-3 theta-isogeny tool (Lubicz-Robert / Milio avisogenies-style), read the 36 even theta-nulls of the codomain. KILL CRITERION: an even theta-null VANISHES (=> hyperelliptic) on the example => by genericity the universal lead is dead for the exponent, keep only constants. If none vanishes (=> plane quartic) on 2-3 independent examples, escalate to building the divisor-map transfer and a priced end-to-end solve.
proposals.quick_check_done: Pure-Python exact enumeration (/tmp/claude-0/-home-user/c9b2fe43-c085-5dfa-9cde-b0311430c5d1/scratchpad/wf/g3transfer/lagr.py, orbit.py): J[2] has 63 nonzero elts (28 weight-2, 35 weight-4); 135 Lagrangians = 105 with weight-multiset (2,2,2,2,4,4,4) [pair/perfect-matching] + 30 all-weight-4 [affine]; under Frobenius (x->x+1 on 7 finite branch points, fix infinity) exactly 2 Lagrangians are stable, BOTH affine, each a single 7-cycle on its 7 nonzero points (=> kernel over F_{q^7}), no fixed nonzero point (consistent with odd #J). Structural proof that 0 pair-type are stable: a pair-type kernel is a perfect matching of the 8 branch points; the unique Frobenius-fixed branch point (infinity) would need a fixed partner, impossible. Simplicity (prime #J) => quotient is a Jacobian, hyperelliptic XOR quartic (decomposable excluded).

dead_ends_found: Pair-type (Smith / perfect-matching) rational (2,2,2)-kernels for prime-order genus-3 (odd-degree model): structurally 0, not merely 0 by census. A pair-type kernel is a perfect matching of the 8 branch points; for prime order f is irreducible of degree 7 so Frobenius has cycle type (7,1), and the unique fixed branch point (infinity) cannot be matched to a fixed partner. Proved by my enumeration (0 of 135 stable pair-type) and matches smith_near_prime_20261114/RESULTS.md (k=1: 0 of 1110) and smith_even_census_20261115. Smith's quartic-producing construction is therefore unavailable for prime order by a theorem, not a statistic.

Decomposable codomain (transfer a genus-3 DL to elliptic/abelian-surface DLs) for prime order: impossible. #J prime => J is F_q-simple => every F_q-isogenous quotient J/L is simple => indecomposable ppav => a genus-3 Jacobian (hyperelliptic XOR plane quartic), never a product. So the attractive 'split into elliptic curves' route cannot occur for prime order.

Odd-l transfer at l=7 (and likely l=5): the rational kernel lives over F_{q^342} (l=7), so even though the transfer is formally poly(log q) for fixed l, the Cantor-over-F_{q^342} plus poly(l^3) theta constant almost certainly exceeds the q^(1/3) head-room over 2LP at any feasible q. Only l=3 (ext deg 13) is worth a look. Source: L06 DERIVATION sec 6 / SPEC ext_deg.

Citing the lab's existing quartic IC/rho numbers as evidence the transfer destination beats q^(4/3): invalid. Those rows are on the GHS-weak E0/F_{q^3} family (4 | #E0, never prime order) or set-up-dominated tiny p, and the quartic negation-rho is overpriced ~1.73x (L10 F_Q, plus a <rho> class-walk factor 0.447). The destination's advantage for GENERIC prime-order quartics is unestablished (problems/quartic-matched-rho-overpricing.md, status open).

GHS / Weil-restriction cover routes to a quartic for prime-order targets: dead by structure (GHS-weak quartic family never prime order; odd-char GHS covers have genus >= 9/49/41; cover_descent_genus_floor_20261015). Not part of g3-transfer but worth excluding as an alternative to the (l,l,l) isogeny.

Trying to settle the affine-type codomain type by pure combinatorics (no curve): impossible. The vanishing of an even theta-null of J/L depends on the actual theta constants (curve moduli), not on the Lagrangian's combinatorics alone, so one explicit isogeny computation on a concrete curve is unavoidable (though one suffices, by S_8-genericity of the 30 affine Lagrangians).

proposals.direction:
nonhyp-diem: improvements to Diem's index calculus for non-hyperelliptic curves (plane quartics, canonical genus-4 curves, low-degree plane/special-linear-system models over prime fields).

Core reframing (contrarian): the lab's genus>=2 program has spent its effort on the HARD non-hyperelliptic win -- transferring a HYPERELLIPTIC target to a plane quartic via Smith/Tian isogenies -- and that route is essentially closed for prime order (lab: 0 of 1110 odd-degree and 0 of 168 even-degree prime-order genus-3 pair kernels are rational, research/smith_near_prime_20261114 + smith_even_census_20261115 via the review; and Naranjo-Pirola 2018 kills any generic transfer for g>=4, cited research/ic_genus2_16_speedup_20261117/research/D_nonhyperelliptic.md sec 5e). But the SAME exponent win is available for FREE on DIRECTLY non-hyperelliptic targets, which are generic and abundant over prime fields -- and the lab has never cleanly measured IC on a prime-order, prime-field non-hyperelliptic Jacobian against a correctly-priced matched rho. That gap, not a new algorithm, is where the biggest exponent margins in the lab's reach are sitting.

The exponent in every fixed-genus Diem-family method is 2-2/e where e is the residual degree (points that must land in the factor base); lowering e is the only exponent lever (D_nonhyperelliptic.md sec 6, cross-cutting conclusion 1). Lines through 2 factor-base points on a degree-d plane model give e=d-2; canonical hyperplanes give e=g-1; Diem-Kochinke pencils give e=g-2; hyperelliptic 2LP gives e=g. Proposals below attack the two residual regimes the lab can actually measure (g=3 quartic e=2 -> exponent 1; g=4 canonical e=3 -> exponent 4/3) and scope the one genuine below-Diem lever (pencils, e=g-2).

proposals.title: Prime-order, prime-field NON-HYPERELLIPTIC genus-3 (smooth plane quartic) index calculus vs a correctly-priced matched rho -- the lab's largest reachable exponent gap (q vs q^1.5)
proposals.mechanism: Target a genus-3 group that is ALREADY a smooth plane quartic over F_p (so NO isogeny transfer is needed, unlike the closed Smith/Tian route). Run Diem's line index calculus: factor base = ~q^(1/2) rational points; draw the line through two base/large-prime points P1,P2; by Bezout L.C = P1+P2+R with R an effective degree-(d-2)=degree-2 residual; record a relation when R splits into two rational points (one quadratic-root test). Double-large-prime graph combines ~q candidate lines into ~q^(1/2) full relations; sparse linear algebra (SGE + Wiedemann/Lanczos) over a q^(1/2)-dim system; special-q descent of the target. e=d-2=2 gives exponent 1 vs rho's 3/2. The lab already has the arithmetic (src/cryptanalysis/plane_quartic_pic.rs, quartic_ladder.rs); the missing piece is a prime-order prime-field ladder measured against the L10-corrected rho.
proposals.applies_to: Genus 3, non-hyperelliptic (smooth plane quartic) curves over prime fields F_p, prime-order or large-prime-subgroup Jacobians. Does NOT apply to hyperelliptic genus-3 (those need the Smith/Tian transfer, closed for prime order). Targets are generic/abundant: my Part-A computation found large-prime-factor Jacobians at ~47-64% and prime #J at 3-13% among random smooth quartics (tiny p, small samples; vs the Smith route's 0/1110).
proposals.predicted_cost: Exponent O~(q^1) total, all phases: setup/transfer O~(1) (pick+sort ~q^(1/2) base points; no transfer); relation search O~(q) (~q candidate lines, O(polylog q) field ops each: substitute line into the quartic, divide out 2 known roots, one split test; residual split prob ~1/2 confirmed by my Part B ~0.52-0.66); linear algebra O~(q) ((q^(1/2))^2 via Wiedemann); target descent O~(q). Constant/memory: large-prime graph ~370 B/vertex and storage ~q^(3/4) (Laine-Lauter 2015 / Diem talk, literature, unverified). Matched rho = q^(3/2) priced as the <rho> class walk, NOT the plain negation walk (L10).

proposals.title: First implementation of Diem-Kochinke pencils (special linear systems) at genus 5: e=g-2=3, exponent 4/3 -- the largest exponent drop below Diem's canonical method at small genus
proposals.mechanism: For nearly all curves of fixed genus g>=5, Diem-Kochinke generate relations from a positive-dimensional family of pencils (special linear systems g^1_d / a g^1 inside a W^1_d) chosen so that members through the prescribed factor-base points have residual degree g-2 instead of the canonical g-1. For g=5 this is e=3, exponent 2-2/(g-2)=4/3, below the canonical 3/2 and far below rho q^2.5. There is NO public implementation; building one -- the construction of the rational pencil family over F_p and the residual/split engine -- is itself the deliverable. This is the only route known to beat Diem's canonical exponent at a genus the lab could in principle instrument.
proposals.applies_to: Genus 5 (and heuristically g>=5) non-hyperelliptic curves over F_p, 'nearly all' curves (Diem-Kochinke heuristic; the method provably FAILS for hyperelliptic curves because the g^1_2 composes everything). Prime-order or large-prime subgroup.
proposals.predicted_cost: Asymptotic exponent O~(q^(2-2/(g-2))) = O~(q^(4/3)) at g=5, all phases: pencil-family construction O~(1) in q but poly(g) and genuinely nontrivial over F_p; factor base ~q^(1-1/(g-2))=q^(2/3); relation search O~(q^(4/3)) (members of the pencil through base points, residual-(g-2)=3 split prob ~1/6); LA O~(q^(4/3)); descent O~(q^(4/3)). vs canonical 3/2 and rho 2.5.

dead_ends_found: Pencils of conics/cubics through factor-base points as a literal relation source to LOWER the exponent on a fixed plane model: DEAD. A degree-m plane curve meets a degree-d model in md points; through k forced points the residual is md-k. The space of degree-m plane curves has dimension m(m+3)/2, so forcing more points requires larger m, which RAISES the residual md-k, not lowers it. Lines (m=1, through 2 points, residual d-2) are optimal among COMPLETE linear systems of plane curves. The genuine Diem-Kochinke win comes from INCOMPLETE special linear systems (g^1_d / g^2_d with extra base-locus structure), not from higher-degree plane curves -- so 'conics/cubics through FB points' as named does not help; verified by the residual-degree arithmetic (D_nonhyperelliptic.md sec 2a, sec 6).

An exponent BELOW q for genus-3 plane quartics (e<2): DEAD / no known route. Beating Diem's O~(q) needs residual degree e=1 (only one point must land in the base), i.e. a line through 3 factor-base points on the quartic. A line has only 2 degrees of freedom, so it cannot be forced through a 3rd point generically; the special lines that do pass through a 3rd rational point are exactly the ordinary e=2 splits already counted, and number only ~q^(1/2), too few and not cheaper to find. The literature records nothing below q for quartics and argues O~(q) is optimal for double-large-prime line IC (D_nonhyperelliptic.md sec 9: 'any improvement of the exponent for genus-3 quartics below 1: not found').

Reaching the non-hyperelliptic genus-3 exponent win by TRANSFERRING hyperelliptic genus-3 targets (Smith (2,2,2) / Tian (l,l,l)): effectively DEAD for prime order in the lab, which is why Proposals 1-2 go after directly non-hyperelliptic targets instead. Lab census: 0 of 1110 odd-degree and 0 of 168 even-degree PRIME-ORDER genus-3 hyperelliptic Jacobians have a rational Smith pair kernel (research/smith_near_prime_20261114, smith_even_census_20261115 via the review); the (l,l,l) census is still open but the kernel points live over extension degree 13-342 making a toy isogeny hard (g2plus L06). And for g>=4 Naranjo-Pirola 2018 proves a very general hyperelliptic Jacobian is not isogenous to any non-hyperelliptic one, so there is NO generic transfer at all (D_nonhyperelliptic.md sec 5e). Conclusion: the non-hyperelliptic exponent advantage must be taken on curves that are non-hyperelliptic to begin with, not imported from hyperelliptic ones.

The min-degree-plane-model route via an F_q-rational g^2_d (derived exponent 2-2/ceil(2g/3), beats Diem-Kochinke pencils for g>=9): not a near-term lab lever. It is explicitly 'inference, not a published theorem' (D_nonhyperelliptic.md sec 2a), its payoff only overtakes pencils at g>=9, and the 63-bit #J guard forces g=10 down to p=11 (review instrument caveat) where no exponent is measurable; the bottleneck (constructing the rational g^2_d over F_q) is unsolved and un-tooled in the repo.

L(1/3) subexponential methods (Enge-Gaudry, Enge-Gaudry-Thome) for the lab's genus range: DEAD for this goal. They require g -> infinity with log q = o(g^c) (q small relative to g); at fixed g in 3..16 with q -> infinity (the lab's regime), L_{q^g}(1/3) is worse than the polynomial q^(2-2/e) family for all cryptographically relevant q (D_nonhyperelliptic.md sec 4).

proposals.direction: large-prime-theory. VERDICT: For GENERIC prime-order hyperelliptic Jacobians over prime fields, the GTTD exponent 2-2/g is a hard barrier under any large-prime relation structure built on degree-1 places. Rigorous counting (my optimizer /tmp/claude-0/-home-user/c9b2fe43-c085-5dfa-9cde-b0311430c5d1/scratchpad/wf/largeprime/count.py, confirming the closed-form balance) shows: with t large primes, factor base F=q^a, large-prime vertex set V'=q^b, relation cost q^{b+(1-a)(g-t)+t(1-b)}, final LA q^{2a}, and large-prime elimination q^b for t=2 (graph: near-linear via spanning forest) but q^{2b} for t>=3 (3+-uniform hypergraph: sparse Gaussian elimination over V' columns, no graph shortcut). Minimizing max(.) gives exactly 2-2/g at t=2 for every genus, and STRICTLY WORSE (~2-2/(g+1)) for unstructured t>=3. The single-large-prime t=1 is also worse (Theriault 2-4/(2g+1), research/hec_ic_speedup_20261113/PLAN.md:38). The deep obstruction: the number of independent full relations = N_p - rank(incidence) is positive only ABOVE the hypergraph 2-core emergence, which is exactly where linear-time peeling fails; the cheap (peelable) regime yields zero relations. So near-linear-elimination AND nonzero-yield is impossible without ALGEBRAIC structure among the large primes. The one true crack: if an automorphism/Frobenius/RM action supplies large-prime dependencies in closed form (orbit-closed elimination), t=3 reaches 2-2/(g-1) (g=4: 4/3 vs 3/2). That structure lives only on special curves, which are rarely prime order, so it does not touch the generic target. Net: in-lane exponent gains for generic prime-order curves are ruled out by counting; realistic wins are constants on the 2-2/g method (which the lab success criterion counts), plus a speculative special-curve exponent lever. Repo context is [pcc:unverified]; literature exponents are recalled from repo docs (research-kb and the sibling lead atlas were not reachable this session), so no standalone 'not tried in the literature' claim is made.

proposals.title: Orbit-closed triple-large-prime elimination on special-automorphism / RM Jacobians (exponent lever, special curves only)
proposals.mechanism: The sole way to beat 2-2/g in-lane is to raise the large-prime count to t=3 while keeping large-prime elimination near-linear. For a generic curve this is impossible (3-uniform hypergraph kernel needs sparse Gaussian elimination ~ V'^2 = q^2, which dominates). But if the curve carries an explicit automorphism sigma of order m>=3 (or real multiplication by an order O), the degree-1 places fall into sigma-orbits, and a batch of sigma-conjugate 3-almost-smooth divisors supplies CLOSED-FORM dependencies among their large primes (the orbit relation sum_i sigma^i(D) is principal / computable). Those dependencies are read off from the orbit action in O(V') time instead of by elimination, so the q^{2b} term is replaced by q^b. The balance then yields exponent 2-2/(g-1): for g=4 that is 4/3 versus the GTTD 3/2; the structured-t pattern is 2-2/(g-t+2).
proposals.applies_to: Special hyperelliptic families with a rational automorphism of order >=3 or computable RM (e.g. y^2=x^(2g+1)+a when (2g+1)|(p-1), or curves with a known real-multiplication order). NOT generic prime-order curves (trivial Aut={+-1}). Fraction of prime-order instances in these families is the decisive unknown and is likely near zero.
proposals.predicted_cost: relation phase q^{1+(1-a)(g-3)} with a=(g-2)/(g-1); large-prime orbit elimination O(q polylog) (the claim); final LA q^{2a}=q^{2-2/(g-1)}; descent q^{o(1)} per logarithm, same order as the GTTD baseline and charged identically. Total q^{2-2/(g-1)}. g=3: q^1; g=4: q^{4/3}; g=5: q^{8/5}. Every phase charged; the win is real only if orbit elimination is genuinely near-linear (the open point).
proposals.prior_work_check: Lab: L02 folds the FACTOR BASE by Aut for a constant m-fold saving and was KILLED at generic genus 3 (pooled IC/rho 1.096 [0.905,1.343] vs bar 2.0), SUPPORTED only narrowly for y^2=x^q+a (research/g2plus_leads_20261116/L02_automorphism_orbit_bases/ASSESSMENT.md). This proposal is distinct: it folds the large-prime ELIMINATION step (an exponent lever via higher t), not the factor base (a constant). Literature: automorphism speedups (Duursma-Gaudry-Morain, Gaudry-Thome-Theriault) are all constant-factor; using the orbit action to cheapen multi-large-prime elimination for an exponent gain is not something I can confirm in the repo and research-kb was unreachable, so label it plausibly-new-but-unverified against the literature, NOT confirmed novel.
proposals.key_risk: The orbit dependencies among large primes may be exactly the 'free' relations that merely reduce the effective large-prime count by m (a constant, collapsing back to L02's dead end), not independent higher-t relations. Worse, curves with extra automorphisms or RM almost always have decomposable or non-prime Jacobians, so the method may never apply to a prime-order target - the same wall that closed Smith (0/1110 odd-degree prime-order admit, research/smith_near_prime_20261114/RESULTS.md).
proposals.cheapest_falsifying_test: Pick one tiny automorphism curve (e.g. y^2=x^7+1 over a small p with 7|p-1, g=3). Enumerate degree-1 places, form their sigma-orbits, generate a few hundred 3-almost-smooth Mumford divisors, build the large-prime incidence matrix, and check EXACTLY (pure Python, <3 min) whether its kernel is recovered from orbit sums in O(V') without Gaussian elimination AND whether those kernel vectors are independent of the m-fold factor-base folding. KILL if (a) the orbit-derived relations are not rank-independent of factor-base folding (then it is L02's constant), or (b) #J of the family is composite for all sampled a (then prime-order target unreachable).

proposals.title: Degree-2 large primes folded into the genus-3/4 double-large-prime graph (constant relation-phase gain)
proposals.mechanism: Keep t<=2 large-prime vertices so elimination stays near-linear (graph), but let one vertex be a DEGREE-2 place rather than two degree-1 places. A reduced divisor with g-2 degree-1 places in F plus one degree-2 place is a single graph edge to a degree-2 vertex; its almost-smooth probability is higher than requiring two degree-1 large primes, so more Cantor trials become usable relations. The graph cycle machinery is unchanged, so LA and elimination costs keep their 2-2/g form; only the relation-phase constant improves.
proposals.applies_to: Genus 3 and 4 hyperelliptic over prime fields, where the lab's actual near-rho rows live. (The lab tested degree-2 large primes only at g>=6.) Any curve; no special structure needed.
proposals.predicted_cost: Exponent unchanged at 2-2/g. Relation phase scaled by a constant c_rel<1 set by the degree-2 smoothness gain minus the cost of a larger (degree-2) vertex set that must be tuned to a subset so the graph still percolates. End-to-end net = c_rel*(relation share) + (LA share unchanged) + (descent unchanged). At genus 3 relation share is ~23-25% (LA is 75-77%, research/genus_ladder_scale_20261115/RESULTS.md via the review), so the ceiling here is modest; at genus 2 relation share dominates (LA 8-20%) so the lever bites harder but genus 2 is already at the rho floor (q^1) and 3-5x above rho with no crossing.

proposals.title: Minimum-weight cycle basis (NFS-style filtering) for the large-prime graph to sparsify the linear-algebra matrix (constant LA gain)
proposals.mechanism: In the double-large-prime graph, each independent cycle becomes one full-relation matrix row whose weight is the sum of the factor-base parts of the edges in the cycle. The lab combines cycles via an arbitrary spanning-forest basis; choosing a SHORT (minimum-weight) cycle basis instead minimizes the resulting rows' average weight, giving a sparser relation matrix and cheaper block-Wiedemann/SGE. This is the hyperelliptic analogue of NFS 'filtering/merge', applied to the large-prime graph cycle-combination step.
proposals.applies_to: Genus 3 and 4 hyperelliptic over prime fields, where LA is the dominant phase (75-77% at g=3). Any curve; composes with the lab's existing SGE and Ferrari levers.
proposals.predicted_cost: Exponent unchanged at 2-2/g. LA phase cost scales with matrix weight; a short-cycle basis reduces average row weight by a constant factor k (cycle-length ratio), cutting the dominant 75-77% LA share by roughly (1-1/k) of its sparse-solver cost. Relation phase and descent unchanged. Net end-to-end constant = (LA share)*(weight reduction) - (one-time min-cycle-basis construction, near-linear, negligible).

proposals.direction: genus2 (prime fields). Verdict: no known route — and none I could identify — beats rho's EXPONENT for generic or prime-order genus-2 Jacobians over prime fields. Genus 2 is exactly the crossover where the best IC exponent equals rho's: double-large-prime IC is Õ(q^{2-2/g}) = q^1 and rho is q^{g/2} = q^1 (repo: research/hec_ic_speedup_20261113/PLAN.md lines 19-30, "Genus 2 can only gain constants. Its best IC exponent equals rho's" [pcc:unverified]; measured: research/genus_ladder_scale_20261115/RESULTS.md gives rho exponent 0.975 [0.908,1.037], 2LP 1.004, ratio 2LP/rho 1.7-5.7 FPM-mid, "no crossing", X4 FAILED). The precise obstruction (below) is that every exponent-moving lever at genus 2 — transfer to an elliptic/lower-genus object, or a low-dimension point-decomposition — is either confined to a measure-zero locus and IMPOSSIBLE for prime-order targets (isogeny preserves #J over F_p, so a split forces composite order), or exists only over extension fields (Weil restriction), which a prime field does not provide. I ran an exact check (660 curves) confirming 0 prime-order genus-2 Jacobians are isogenous to a product. The only honestly-live levers are CONSTANT factors on the relation phase, and the lab's own data says the gap to rho is 3-5x and flat. I therefore submit one obstruction+detector, and two bounded constant-factor proposals, all honestly labeled; I do not claim any exponent breakthrough, because none is available and fabricating one would violate the no-inflation rule.

proposals.title: Precise exponent obstruction + O((log p)^c) weak-curve detector (split Jacobian / elliptic subcover)
proposals.mechanism: The ONLY route that moves the genus-2 exponent below q^1 is transferring the prime-order-N DLP into an elliptic curve. This requires J isogenous over F_p to a product E1 x E2 (or a cover J -> E), so that the N-torsion injects into an elliptic factor over F_p, where rho is q^{1/2} (exponent 1 -> 1/2). Detector: compute Frobenius charpoly P(T)=T^4 - s1 T^3 + s2 T^2 - p s1 T + p^2 from #C(F_p),#C(F_{p^2}); if it factors into two Hasse-valid integer quadratics (T^2-aT+p)(T^2-bT+p), then J ~ E1 x E2 with #J=#E1*#E2, and if N | #E_i the DLP collapses to the prime field elliptic curve. Also flag RM/CM and automorphism structure. The obstruction: isogeny preserves #J over F_p (an isogeny invariant), so ANY A isogenous to J has #A=#J; if A=E1 x E2 then #J=#E1*#E2 is composite. Hence a prime-order J is absolutely simple and never splits, and no (l,l)-isogeny / Richelot neighbor (all genus 2, same N) and no cover to lower genus can exist. For non-prime-order J, split is possible only on the Humbert/split modular locus, a codimension-1 (measure-zero) subvariety of M_2.
proposals.applies_to: All genus-2 hyperelliptic curves over prime fields. The exponent collapse applies ONLY to the measure-zero split/elliptic-subcover locus and NEVER to prime-order (cryptographic) Jacobians. The detector is a universal, negligible-cost hygiene filter.
proposals.predicted_cost: Detector: one point-count pair + one quartic factorization = O((log p)^c) field ops, negligible vs any solve. On a positive hit (measure-zero curves): attack is p^{1/2} (elliptic rho on the prime field) + O(1) isogeny evaluation. On the generic/prime-order case: detector returns NEGATIVE and the exponent stays q^1 for both IC and rho (all phases: relation ~p, descent, LA 8-20%, set-up).
proposals.baseline_beaten: rho q^1 -> q^{1/2} on split/subcover curves only (literature; repo cover-attack framing in research/cover_descent_genus_floor_20261015 and L07 Prym desk count). For prime-order targets it beats nothing — it proves nothing can.
proposals.prior_work_check: Known in literature: elliptic subfields/subcovers (Kani-Rosen; Frey-Rück style transfers; Gaudry-Hess-Smart cover attacks). Checking for elliptic subcovers / absolute simplicity is standard cryptographic hygiene. Lab: genus-3 analogue closed by census (smith_near_prime/smith_even_census, 0 of 1110+168 prime-order curves admit the Smith transfer); genus-2 split-locus obstruction is not separately written up in the reviewed dirs, so the detector-as-filter + the exact prime-order-vs-split demonstration is new-in-lab, but the mathematics is classical.
proposals.key_risk: It is an obstruction, not an attack: ~0 of cryptographic targets are affected. Risk of over-selling as a 'route' — it is the precise reason there is no route. Secondary: geometrically-split-but-F_p-simple curves (charpoly irreducible over Q, factors over an extension) still have #J=#A for any F_p-isogenous A, so the order argument still forbids prime order; the extension-field elliptic factor lives over F_{p^k}, k>=2, giving rho p^{k/2} >= p^{1}, no gain.
proposals.cheapest_falsifying_test: DONE. /tmp/claude-0/-home-user/c9b2fe43-c085-5dfa-9cde-b0311430c5d1/scratchpad/wf/genus2/obstruction.py: 660 random genus-2 curves y^2=f(x), deg f=5, over p in {11..47}. Result: prime_order=35, split=107, split_product_matches_#J=107/107, split_AND_prime=0. Kill criterion for the obstruction (as a theorem): exhibit a single prime-order genus-2 J over F_p isogenous to a product — none found, and the order-invariance theorem says none exists. Kill criterion for the detector's usefulness: if a sampled 'cryptographic' (prime-order) population ever shows a positive hit.
proposals.quick_check_done: 660-curve exact computation above: 0/35 prime-order curves split; 107/107 split curves have #J = #E1*#E2 exactly (verifies both isogeny order-invariance and the composite-order consequence).

proposals.title: Automorphism-orbit factor base with set-up amortized across the orbit, matched against a GLV/GLS-accelerated rho (special families y^2=x^5+a, x^6+a)
proposals.mechanism: On curves with an efficiently computable order-m automorphism over F_p (e.g. y^2=x^5+a with the zeta_5 action at p=1 mod 5), one relation generates an orbit of m relations at O(1) marginal cost (classical; Duursma-Gaudry-Morain). L02 measured 2.46x [2.23,2.75] at genus 2 but the assessor found ~80% of the apparent advantage is rho walk-start/jump-table SET-UP, and the net shrinks to 1.6-2.0x once set-up is removed from both sides. Proposal: amortize the dominant walk-start/jump-table set-up ONCE per orbit in the IC relation phase, AND match against a rho that uses the SAME automorphism (GLV/GLS), so neither side is flattered by set-up accounting. Measure the honest residual orbit gain.
proposals.applies_to: Measure-zero special families with a rational, efficiently computable automorphism over the prime field (y^2=x^5+a, y^2=x^6+a and similar). Prime order is possible within these families but rare. Exponent q^1 unchanged; constant only.
proposals.predicted_cost: Exponent p^1. Relation phase cut ~m-fold in orbit-yield but matched GLV-rho also speeds ~sqrt(m); set-up paid once per orbit on the IC side. Net target: beat L02's honest 1.6-2.0x residual; realistic prior is a near-wash (~1-2x) because the matched automorphism-rho absorbs most of the gain.
proposals.baseline_beaten: L02 net 1.6-2.0x (research/g2plus_leads_20261116/L02_automorphism_orbit_bases/ASSESSMENT.md), and the general genus-2 arm-c 1.7-5.7x (genus_ladder_scale). A verified residual >1 across the §5a band against GLV-rho would be a (narrow-family) constant success.

dead_ends_found: Kummer-surface relation walk: accelerates the group operation (Cantor step) that BOTH IC and rho use, and rho — a pure differential-addition scalar walk — benefits at least as much (Gaudry's fast Kummer rho/kangaroo). So it cannot change the genus-2 IC/rho ratio. The lab's measured gap is the NUMBER of walk steps (~p relations) and collision/cycle bookkeeping, not per-step arithmetic (research/genus_ladder_scale_20261115/RESULTS.md: 'the cost is the relation walk'). Dead end for a relative lever.

Summation-polynomial / Semaev / Nagao point-decomposition index calculus: gives sub-rho exponents (Õ(q^{2-2/n})) only over EXTENSION fields F_{q^n} via Weil restriction, where the decomposition dimension n grows (Gaudry, Diem, Nagao). A prime field is n=1: no Weil restriction, and the genus-2 Jacobian decomposition sits in dimension g=2, fixing the exponent at 2-2/g = 1. No prime-field gain. Dead end with precise reason.

Richelot / (l,l)-isogeny transfer to a 'curve with extra structure': an isogeny over F_p preserves #J (isogeny invariant), so every (2,2)/(l,l) neighbor of a prime-order J is again a genus-2 Jacobian with the SAME prime order and the SAME q^1 IC. No neighbor can be a product (that needs composite order). Confirmed exactly: /tmp/claude-0/-home-user/c9b2fe43-c085-5dfa-9cde-b0311430c5d1/scratchpad/wf/genus2/obstruction.py, 107/107 split curves have composite #J. Dead end for the exponent.

Cover mapping genus-2 DLP into a low-degree plane model: a genus-2 curve has gonality 2 and no smooth plane model (smooth plane degree d has genus (d-1)(d-2)/2, never 2). Diem's plane-curve exponent 2-2/(d-2) is below 1 only for d<4, and d=3 forces genus<=1 — i.e. an elliptic subcover, which makes the Jacobian split, hence composite order, excluded by prime order. No admissible low-degree plane model exists. Dead end, matches L07's Prym desk-count kill (16/9, 20/11 > hyperelliptic bar).

Degree-2-place factor base to raise the smoothness probability (fewer walk steps): raising split probability toward 1 by admitting degree-2 places blows the factor base to ~p^2/2 and makes LA dominate. Lab arms D/E show degree-2/degree-3 bases pay only at g>=6 (research/ic_genus2_16_speedup_20261117, P1/P2); at g=2 it is a loss. Dead end, lab-confirmed.

Any pure accounting/relabelling route (e.g. re-pricing rho, choosing a looser rho reference, removing set-up from only one side): forbidden by the owner's success criterion ('relabelling and accounting changes are not improvements'), and the L02 assessor shows set-up asymmetry already fabricates ~80% of an apparent orbit gain. Not a lever.

proposals.direction: Linear algebra and factor-base shape for genus >= 3 prime-field index calculus. Finding: at the lab's only below-rho hyperelliptic row (validated genus-4 prime-order, research/genus4_prime_order_20261118), linear algebra is 56% (p=16411) and 60% (p=32771) of w=1 native cost even after the cc x SGE tuning, and that LA cost is ~2*dim*nnz dominated by +/-1 vector ADDITIONS in a length-2N coordinate-Wiedemann sequence (verified: la_wied_add/[2*dim*nnz] = 0.96-0.98). The genus_ladder binary uses coordinate Wiedemann on a RANDOM square row subset, while the lab already has a validated block-Lanczos LA in its separate GHS-weak quartic lane. So the highest-value in-lane moves are (1) port block Lanczos into the genus_ladder LA (halves the 2N SpMV sequence to ~N) and (2) replace the random square subset with weight-aware relation selection/purge from the 3.6x excess. Both are measured CONSTANT improvements on an unchanged exponent; neither moves the 2-2/g = 1.5 double-large-prime exponent, which is a proven floor for degree-1-place IC at fixed genus (GTTD 2007). No LA or factor-base lever reaches an exponent at fixed genus, and over PRIME fields the Frobenius/automorphism factor-base quotient that helps over extension fields gives nothing (all degree-1 places rational, generic curves have no automorphisms). Genus 3 (LA share 75-77%) is the higher-leverage target for the same Lanczos port and is the cheapest shot at resolving genus-3 IC below rho at w=1.

proposals.title: Block Lanczos in the genus-ladder binary, replacing coordinate Wiedemann for the mod-r sparse solve
proposals.mechanism: The validated genus-4 result is produced by src/bin/genus_ladder, whose LA is ic_control::wiedemann_coord: coordinate Wiedemann on a random square row subset, run as a length-2N scalar sequence of full sparse mat-vec products. I verified from the raw run records that its dominant counter la_wied_add ~= 2*dim*nnz (ratio 0.959 at p=16411, 0.978 at p=32771) and that la_add is ~91% of all LA ops, i.e. the cost is 2N SpMV accumulations over a matrix whose entries are mostly +/-1. Block Lanczos (Montgomery 1995; Montgomery-style block over a large prime) solves the same system in ~N iterations of one block-SpMV each, i.e. ~N SpMV-equivalents versus Wiedemann's 2N, plus O(b*dim*N) dense b x b work (sub-leading for block width b=4). Net LA op-count ~0.5-0.6x. The lab ALREADY has this: a validated block-Lanczos LA (width 4, with the M-orthogonality product reuse) in its GHS-weak quartic lane (docs/ic-leaderboard.html sections ghs-weak-blreuse-20261115, ghs-weak-nrmlz-20261115). The proposal is to wire that existing LA into the genus_ladder Wiedemann slot for genus 2-5 hyperelliptic.
proposals.applies_to: Genus 3, 4, 5 hyperelliptic Jacobians over prime fields, prime order included (r is a 56-60 bit prime; block Lanczos breakdown probability ~dim/r ~ 2e3/2^56 is negligible). Highest leverage at genus 3 (LA is 75-77% of the 2LP cost per the review of genus_ladder_scale_20261115) and genus 4 (LA 56-60% at the tuned cc=1.4). Does NOT help genus 2 (LA only 8-20%).
proposals.predicted_cost: End-to-end certified solve counts (relation + LA + target descent are all in the recorded counts; setup/factor-base build is O(base), small). Phase shares at the genus-4 x* row, p=16411: group 0.3%, relation 43.7%, LA 56.0%. Charging LA at 0.5-0.6x of current and holding relation fixed: total multiplier 0.72-0.78, so IC/ideal-negation-rho at w=1 moves 0.876 -> 0.63-0.68 (p=16411) and 0.640 -> 0.45-0.49 (p=32771). Exponent (slope of ln(IC/rho) in ln p) stays ~ -0.45 (IC cost ~ p^1.54, rho p^2); the LA share rises with p (0.56->0.60) so the constant gain grows slightly with p, nudging the slope marginally steeper but NOT changing the 1.5 exponent. At measured wall weights (w_la ~ 0.004 GAE, genus4_cost_calibration_20261119) LA is ~1.5s of 2.5s wall, so the ~2x LA op cut is also a genuine ~1.4x wall-time win, not only a w=1-ledger gain.

proposals.prior_work_check: Literature: block Lanczos for sparse systems over finite fields is standard in NFS/FFS (Montgomery 1995; LaMacchia-Odlyzko), ~N vs Wiedemann 2N mat-vecs. Lab: block Lanczos is IMPLEMENTED and VALIDATED in the GHS-weak quartic lane but the genus>=2 hyperelliptic genus_ladder binary still uses coordinate Wiedemann (grep: src/cryptanalysis/genus_ladder.rs calls wiedemann_coord / wiedemann; Lanczos code lives in other modules and the quartic lane). So this is KNOWN in literature and EXISTS in the lab, but is UNTESTED in the genus-ladder lane that owns every genus 2-5 hyperelliptic row. Not a new algorithm; a port plus a measured constant.
proposals.key_risk: (1) The ~2x is a mat-vec-count estimate; the lab's coordinate Wiedemann is already the lean 2N-sequence variant (no separate N-length solution-evaluation pass), so the realized factor could be closer to 0.6x than 0.5x, and block Lanczos's dense b x b bookkeeping (~15% of the halved cost at b=4, dim~2000) eats into the win. (2) Block Lanczos needs the matrix made symmetric/square (A^T A or a self-orthogonal block); over a 56-60 bit prime this is fine but adds a transpose-apply per iteration (keeps the ~N*nnz leading term). (3) It is a constant, not an exponent: it will not flip genus 2 (3-5x above rho) and may not, by itself, push genus 3 below rho at w=1 if the genus-3 w=1 IC/rho is well above 1.
proposals.cheapest_falsifying_test: Export one genus-4 core matrix at p=16411 (dim~2007, nnz~27641) from a single genus_ladder run (the binary already records core rows/cols/nnz; add a one-off dump or reconstruct from the relation log). In pure Python/numpy mod r, run a reference block-Lanczos (width 1-4) and count SpMV applications to a kernel vector; compare against the recorded la_wied_add/nnz ~= 2*dim. proposals.title: Weight-aware relation selection (purge) from the 3.6x excess, replacing the random square row subset
proposals.mechanism: genus_ladder collects a large relation excess then solves coordinate Wiedemann 'on a random square row subset' (src/cryptanalysis/genus_ladder.rs doc for wiedemann_coord). At the genus-4 x* row the binary gathers ~7377 relations but the core is ~2035 rows (a ~3.6x excess), and the square subset is chosen RANDOMLY, so the matrix weight is the average relation weight, not the minimum achievable. Standard NFS/FFS filtering (Cavallar 2000; CADO-NFS purge+merge) instead (a) removes singletons, (b) prunes by a clique/large-prime-graph pass, and (c) keeps the sparsest relations, minimizing dim*nnz directly rather than merging low-weight columns greedily by shortest pivot (the current SGE). Because LA cost ~2*dim*nnz is add-dominated, cutting nnz by choosing the sparsest ~28% of the excess translates straight into LA savings and composes with Proposal 1.
proposals.applies_to: Same regime as Proposal 1 (genus 3-5 hyperelliptic, LA-dominated). Depends on having real relation excess; the genus-4 runs show 3.6x, so the lever is live there. Modest and only where the collected excess is large and the current core selection is random/arrival-order.
proposals.predicted_cost: If weight-aware selection cuts core nnz ~15-20% (plausible when picking the sparsest 28% of relations), LA -> ~0.80-0.85x at fixed dim. On the genus-4 x* row (LA share 0.56/0.60) that is a total multiplier 0.89-0.92 -> IC/ideal-negation-rho 0.876 -> ~0.78-0.81 (p=16411), 0.640 -> ~0.57-0.59 (p=32771) on its own. Combined with Proposal 1 (f_LA ~ 0.41): 0.876 -> ~0.59 (p=16411), 0.640 -> ~0.41 (p=32771). Relation phase cost rises negligibly (selection is a sort over already-collected relations; no extra search). Setup/descent unchanged.

The current SGE(4,1.5) only merged 164 of 2001 columns and slightly RAISED nnz (26872 -> 27422 in the inspected run), confirming the column-merge lever is near-dead here while the row-selection lever is untouched.

Lab: the genus_ladder lane does singleton peeling (sge_peeled) and greedy column SGE, but selects the square subset randomly and does not minimize matrix cost by relation choice; the GHS-weak lane does more LA tuning but not this specific row-selection step. So KNOWN in literature, only partially present in the lab, and the specific 'sparsest subset instead of random subset' step is untested. dead_ends_found: Frobenius / automorphism quotient of the factor base over PRIME fields: gives nothing. The IC factor base is the degree-1 places (points up to the hyperelliptic involution, which is already used to halve the base). Over F_p all degree-1 places are rational, so Frobenius acts trivially and provides no orbit quotient; generic prime-order curves have no extra automorphisms (the lab's L02 closed automorphism-orbit bases except for special families y^2=x^q+a). The large Frobenius/Galois quotient that shrinks factor bases over EXTENSION fields (GHS/Gaudry/Diem settings) is simply absent in the prime-field regime that is the goal.

Block Wiedemann (as opposed to block Lanczos) as an op-count lever: block Wiedemann does ~2*dim/b block-mat-vecs of b vectors each = ~2*dim*nnz work total, the SAME leading op-count as the current scalar coordinate Wiedemann, plus Coppersmith generator overhead. It is a parallelism / wall-clock lever (shares the sequence across SIMD lanes/cores), not an op-count reduction, so it earns nothing in the w=1 ledger and cannot be measured honestly on the current busy 4-vCPU host (timing invalid during the running search). Block LANCZOS, by contrast, genuinely halves the SpMV count (Proposal 1).

Re-pricing the linear algebra to its measured wall weight (w_la ~ 0.004 GAE, genus4_cost_calibration_20261119) to report IC as ~0.4-0.6% of rho: this is an accounting/relabelling change, explicitly disallowed by the success criterion ('Relabelling and accounting changes are not improvements'), and the lab already reports the full w in {0,0.1,1} band. Not an improvement.

Any exponent gain at fixed genus from LA or factor-base shape: barred. The double-large-prime exponent 2-2/g (=1.5 at genus 4, 4/3 at genus 3) is a proven floor for degree-1-place index calculus at fixed genus (Gaudry-Thome-Theriault-Diem 2007). cc (base-size constant), SGE/merge, purge, and the iterative solver are all sub-leading constants in front of this exponent; none changes it. Exponent movement at genus 3 needs the transfer to a plane quartic (Diem q^1), which is a different lane (and 0% of prime-order curves are Smith-admissible per the lab census).

Mod-r CRT / smaller-modulus linear algebra: the target regime is PRIME-ORDER Jacobians, so r is a single 56-60 bit prime. There is no composite structure to split the solve across smaller moduli, so CRT-style LA speedups (useful when the group order factors) do not apply.

Pushing SGE deeper (column merging at w_max=8,16,32 / fill_max=2,3,4): already in the validated x* tuning grid (tune.py over SGE in {(4,1.5),(8,2),(16,3),(32,4)}) and REJECTED - the w=1 optimum picked the mildest SGE(4,1.5) because the merge fill shows up as la_add and LA is add-dominated (2*dim*nnz), so deeper column merges raise the w=1 cost. The LA headroom is in the solver (Lanczos) and in row selection (purge), not in more aggressive column merging.

proposals.direction: Cross-genus transfers over prime fields: map a genus-g Jacobian DLP to a curve with a lower-degree plane model / lower gonality where Diem-type index calculus is cheaper. The unifying finding is that the cheap case needs NO transfer: the GENERIC genus-g curve over F_p is non-hyperelliptic, and its native plane/gonality model already gives a smaller IC exponent than the hyperelliptic 2LP bar the lab measures. Transfers are only needed for the measure-zero hyperelliptic sublocus, and for prime-order targets simplicity forces any transfer to land on another g-dimensional Jacobian (generically non-hyperelliptic). All repo numbers cited are [pcc:unverified] per the repo's own standing (no replay cert, no VALIDATION.json, no matched-rho at the section-5a band for any genus>=2 prime-field row except the genus-4 validated-with-errata study).

proposals.title: Native Diem plane-quartic IC on generic prime-order non-hyperelliptic genus-3 Jacobians (no transfer): exponent 1 at density ~1
proposals.mechanism: A smooth plane quartic C/F_p is a genus-3 curve of gonality 3 whose OWN degree-4 plane model is the input to Diem's line-relation index calculus. DLP in Pic^0(C) is solved in O~(q)=O~(p) (lines through pairs of factor-base points; genus from (d-1)(d-2)/2=3). The map is the identity: the generic genus-3 Jacobian is already a plane quartic, so the 'transfer to a plane quartic' the owner's goal assumes is only needed for the hyperelliptic (gonality-2) sublocus, which is dimension 5 in the dimension-6 moduli space M_3 (density ->0). Contrarian point: the lab has spent its genus-3 effort on measure-zero hyperelliptic->quartic transfers (Smith, L06) while the density-1 non-hyperelliptic case gives exponent 1 for free.
proposals.applies_to: Non-hyperelliptic genus-3 curves over F_p = generic locus of M_3 (density ->1 among genus-3 Jacobians). Prime order occurs with density ~1/ln(p^3) (my computation). No cofactor restriction; the input is the curve's native plane model.
proposals.predicted_cost: Every phase at q=p: setup (factor base ~q points) O~(q); relation search (Diem lines, 4 intersection roots each) O~(q); linear algebra sparse q x q mod r via Wiedemann/Lanczos q^{1+o(1)} -- THIS is the load-bearing requirement; target descent O~(polylog). Total O~(q)=O~(p), exponent 1. Constant is large (quartic Pic op ~3523 mult + 44 inv per repo w1_canonical in research/genus_ladder_20261114/RESULTS.md), so the win is exponent, not constant.
proposals.prior_work_check: Algorithm is Diem 2006 / Diem-Thome 2008 (literature, recalled in research/g2plus_leads_20261116/L08_.../PROTOCOL.md lines 55-57 and confirmed as a 'measurement of a known result' in research/plane_quartic_program_20261018/CLOSING.md). Lab has measured Diem quartic IC only on (a) the GHS-weak E/F_{q^3} descent family, which is NEVER prime order (research/plane_quartic_program_20261018/CLOSING.md; crossover q*=555 in M-eq, special family) and (b) one generic-quartic cell at p=1031, set-up-dominated, exponent fit 0.69, with matched rho overpriced 1.73x (research/genus_ladder_20261114/RESULTS.md row 'plane quartic g=3' 0.027[0.019,0.037]; L10 F_Q=1.73 in research/g2plus_leads_20261116/L10_c34_picard_matched_rho/ASSESSMENT.md). NO prime-order, prime-field, decisive-scale, fully-charged measurement with corrected rho exists. Beats docs/ACTIVE.md goal baselines: rho q^{3/2} and 2LP q^{4/3} on genus 3.
proposals.key_risk: Linear-algebra exponent. If the quartic lane uses dense/structured Gaussian elimination instead of a sparse solver, LA cost ~q^{2} dominates and the q^1 advantage evaporates -- exactly the L08 failure mode. Second risk: the matched rho must be the L10-corrected <rho> class walk (0.447x of the overpriced negation walk), or the IC/rho ratio is flattered and the comparison is rejected at the gate. Reachable p is capped near 2e6 by the 63-bit #J guard, a ~2000x lever arm from p=1031.

proposals.title: (l,l,l)-isogeny transfer for prime-order HYPERELLIPTIC genus 3: codomain type is resolved (generically a plane quartic), computability of the isogeny is the only real blocker
proposals.mechanism: For a prime-order hyperelliptic genus-3 Jacobian J/F_p (the cryptographically-chosen, measure-zero case), take the isogeny with a rational Frobenius-stable maximal isotropic (Lagrangian) kernel in J[l]. Structural resolution of the L06 open question: prime order => J simple => the isogenous codomain J' is simple => J' indecomposable; a dimension-3 indecomposable ppav IS a Jacobian (the complement of the Torelli image in A_3 is exactly the decomposable locus, classical for g<=3), and the hyperelliptic Jacobians are a codimension-1 sublocus, so J' is GENERICALLY a plane quartic. Then Diem q^1 on J'. This closes the 'is the codomain a plane quartic?' blocking question in the AFFIRMATIVE generically; what remains is whether the isogeny is computable.
proposals.applies_to: Prime-order hyperelliptic genus-3 curves over F_p carrying a rational Frobenius-stable Lagrangian in J[l] whose kernel points live over a SMALL extension F_{p^k}. Rational Lagrangians have positive density (research/g2plus_leads_20261116/L06_.../ASSESSMENT_RERUN.md: criterion fires on 167/600, 161/600, 144/600 prime-order curves at l=3,5,7; every odd-order Jac has exactly two rational affine-type Lagrangians). The open quantity is the k-distribution.
proposals.predicted_cost: Transfer: theta-coordinate (l,l,l)-isogeny evaluation, poly(l,k) * (cost of arithmetic over F_{p^k}); AFFORDABLE only if k=O(polylog p). Then Diem q^1 on the quartic codomain (phases as in Proposal 1). If k ~ l^2 (up to 342 per the L06 review) the transfer is super-polynomial and the lead dies for that curve. Net exponent 1 (vs 2LP q^{4/3}, rho q^{3/2}) on the computable sub-family only.
proposals.prior_work_check: Smith 2008 established the l=2 case (codomain generically non-hyperelliptic quartic); the indecomposability=>Jacobian=>generically-non-hyperelliptic argument is the natural odd-l generalization and the theta-isogeny machinery is literature (Cosset-Robert, Lubicz-Robert). In the lab: Smith (2,2,2) pair kernels give 0 density on prime order (research/smith_near_prime_20261114/RESULTS.md: k=1 Frobenius cycle (7,1) -> 0/1110). L06 odd-l census is void by a miscalibrated gate but its counts stand (research/g2plus_leads_20261116/L06_.../ASSESSMENT_RERUN.md); it left the codomain type and the k-cost OPEN. The structural resolution of the codomain type is not stated in the lab (my contribution); the hard computability part is unsolved everywhere for odd l over prime fields.
proposals.key_risk: Computability / kernel-field degree k. The review's 'k up to 342 at l=7' suggests most prime-order curves are infeasible; whether a POSITIVE-density small-k sub-family exists is unknown. Second risk: no CAS (Sage/PARI/Magma) on the host, so the isogeny prototype must be written from scratch. If small-k curves are vanishingly rare, this reduces to Proposal 1's density-1 non-hyperelliptic case and adds nothing for hyperelliptic targets.
proposals.cheapest_falsifying_test: Cheap exact census, pure Python, no CAS, no isogeny needed: for prime-order hyperelliptic genus-3 curves over small p, compute #J -> Frobenius charpoly chi(T) (degree 6, from a1,a2,a3 via the same N1,N2,N3 point-count machinery already written for the quartic test); for l in {3,5,7} reduce chi mod l, enumerate Frobenius-stable Lagrangians of the symplectic space (F_l)^6, and compute k = order of Frobenius restricted to each (= field of definition of the kernel points). KILL the lead if < 5% of prime-order curves have a rational Lagrangian with k <= 4 (no affordable computable sub-family). This is a ~1-2 minute computation and decides the lead without building a single isogeny.

proposals.title: Generic-genus ladder: native degree-(g+1) nodal plane model gives Diem exponent 2-2/(g-1), beating the hyperelliptic 2LP bar 2-2/g for every g>=3, with a corrected instrument
proposals.mechanism: The generic genus-g curve over F_p is non-hyperelliptic; projecting its canonical model from a general point yields a plane model of degree g+1 with (g-1)(g-2)/2 nodes, on which Diem line-relation IC costs O~(q^{2-2/(g-1)}). Since 2-2/(g-1) < 2-2/g (hyperelliptic 2LP) and < g/2 (rho) for all g>=3, the generic Jacobian's NATIVE model beats both baselines in exponent with no transfer. This generalizes Proposal 1 (g=3: 1 vs 4/3 vs 3/2) up the ladder: g=4 gives 4/3 vs 3/2 vs 2; g=5 gives 3/2 vs 8/5 vs 5/2.
proposals.applies_to: Generic (non-hyperelliptic) genus-g curves over F_p, g=4,5,6..., density ->1 among genus-g Jacobians; prime order at density ~1/ln(p^g). The map is the native canonical-projection plane model. Not the hyperelliptic sublocus (there 2LP q^{2-2/g} remains the bar).
proposals.predicted_cost: Per phase at q=p: factor base ~q, relation search O~(q) (lines on a degree-(g+1) model), sparse LA q^{1+o(1)}, descent polylog. Total O~(q^{2-2/(g-1)}). The nodes must be handled in the relation step (singular points excluded from the smooth factor base) but do not change the exponent.
proposals.prior_work_check: Diem plane-degree-d exponent 2-2/(d-2) is literature; the e=g-1 canonical/degree-(g+1) reading is recalled in research/ic_genus2_16_speedup_20261117 note D and research/g2plus_leads_20261116/L08_.../PROTOCOL.md (lines 55-57), both literature-unverified (KB was unavailable). The lab's ONE attempt (L08 non-hyperelliptic ladder g4-g6) is INCONCLUSIVE because duplicate relation lines were counted as useful and LA was charged before large-prime elimination (research/g2plus_leads_20261116/L08_.../ASSESSMENT.md): the apparent d=5 slope 0.981 is an instrument artefact, the d=4 control slope 1.618 failed its own positive control. So the ladder is UNTESTED cleanly. Beats the lab's hyperelliptic genus-g 2LP rows (e.g. genus-4 validated x* fits p^{1.54} ~ 2LP 3/2) on the non-hyperelliptic family.
proposals.key_risk: Same LA-exponent risk as Proposal 1, amplified: at higher g the factor base and relation matrix are larger and sparse LA must be used, or the exponent is lost (precisely what broke L08). Node bookkeeping on the plane model is error-prone (the L08 duplicate-line bug is a cautionary case). And reachable p shrinks with g under the 63-bit #J guard (g=5: p<=~6000 per the review), so the exponent lever arm is short above g=4.
proposals.cheapest_falsifying_test: Re-run the L08 non-hyperelliptic ladder with the two instrument fixes (count DISTINCT relation lines once; charge LA only AFTER large-prime elimination) on generic prime-order curves at g=4 (d=5 model) over a prime ladder, fitting the total-cost exponent with sparse LA. KILL if the corrected g=4 exponent >= 3/2 across the w-band (no gain over hyperelliptic 2LP) or if the d=4 positive control does not recover its known exponent 1. Cheap pre-check (minutes, pure Python): on one small prime, verify that after de-duplication the relation matrix rank grows linearly in the number of DISTINCT lines (if duplicates were the only 'relations', the lead is dead immediately).
proposals.quick_check_done: none for the ladder itself; the exponent arithmetic 2-2/(g-1) < 2-2/g < g/2 for g>=3 is elementary and I verified it by hand for g=3,4,5,6. The L08 artefact is read from the repo, not re-measured.

dead_ends_found: Cover / GHS / Weil-restriction transfers for PRIME-ORDER targets over F_p: structurally dead. There is no base-field extension to descend from over a prime field, odd-characteristic GHS covers of E/GF(p^k) have genus >= 9/49/41 at k=6/10/14 (research/cover_descent_genus_floor_20261015/README.md), the GHS-weak plane-quartic family is never prime order (4 | #E0 over F_{q^3}, research/plane_quartic_program_20261018/CLOSING.md), and Diem's simplicity theorem forces genus >= 7 for a nonzero algebraic transfer. Not a prime-field prime-order route.

Smith (2,2,2) PAIR-kernel transfer for prime-order hyperelliptic genus 3: 0 density. Prime-order odd-degree curves have f irreducible (k=1), Frobenius cycle type (7,1), no Frobenius-stable pairing: 0 of 1110 pass; even-degree prime-order models 0 of 168 (research/smith_near_prime_20261114/RESULTS.md, research/smith_even_census_20261115). Only non-pair and odd-l kernels remain open (Proposal 2).

Prym index calculus on the etale double cover, naive anti-invariant family: exponent 2-2/(2g+1) = 16/9 (g=4), 20/11 (g=5), strictly ABOVE the hyperelliptic bar 2-2/g (research/g2plus_leads_20261116/L07_.../ASSESSMENT.md, KILLED). The Abel-Prym E - sigma E family might reach 2-2/g but not below, so even the optimistic Prym route does not beat the hyperelliptic bar.

Isogeny-decomposition / bielliptic splitting of the DLP (reduce Jac(C) to E x Prym and solve on the smaller factor): impossible for prime-order targets. A prime-order Jacobian is a SIMPLE abelian variety, so it admits no nontrivial isogeny to a product; any transfer must be to another simple g-dimensional ppav of the same order. This is why the only live prime-order transfer is hyperelliptic -> non-hyperelliptic of the SAME genus (Proposal 2).

Genus-2 transfers for an exponent gain: dead. Genus-2 2LP is already q^1 = rho's exponent (group dimension 2); any cheaper IC would need a gonality-1 model, which does not exist. The lab's genus-2 rows are flat at 3-5x above rho with no crossing (review; research/genus_ladder_scale_20261115). Only constants are available at genus 2, not an exponent.

Lowering hyperelliptic gonality: a hyperelliptic curve has gonality 2, already minimal, so no lower-degree map to P^1 exists. Gaudry-type IC on the degree-2 map gives q^{2-2/g}, which is the 2LP bar and is not improvable by choosing a different model of the SAME hyperelliptic curve. The improvement only comes from leaving the hyperelliptic locus (Proposals 1-3).

It is neither: genus_ladder.rs uses coordinate Wiedemann on a random square subset (verified counter la_wied_add ~= 2*dim*nnz, ratio 0.959/0.978 at p=16411/32771, la_add ~91% of LA), while a VALIDATED width-4 block Lanczos already exists in the GHS-weak quartic lane (ic-leaderboard ghs-weak-blreuse). Block Lanczos is ~N SpMV vs Wiedemann's 2N, a real op-count cut (0.5-0.6x), not a wall-clock-only parallelism trick (that would be block WIEDEMANN - correctly listed as a dead end). Pricing band: it cuts counted ops, so it survives at w=1 (not an accounting change). Refutation that stuck partially: it is a CONSTANT, not an exponent - it cannot flip genus 2 (3-5x above rho, no crossing) and may not by itself push genus 3 below rho at w=1 if the g3 w=1 ratio is well above 1; realized factor may be ~0.6x (dense bxb bookkeeping eats ~15% at b=4, dim~2000). But LA is 56-60% of cost at the validated genus-4 x* row and 75-77% at genus 3, so the constant is the highest-leverage in-lane move the lab has.
ranked.surviving_claim: Block Lanczos moves the validated genus-4 x* IC/ideal-negation-rho from 0.876->~0.63-0.68 (p=16411) and 0.640->~0.45-0.49 (p=32771) at w=1, and is the cheapest shot at resolving genus-3 IC below rho at w=1; composes with #1 (quartic lane already has the solver) and with #4.

KILL if SpMV count >= 0.80*(2*dim) (<20% mat-vec reduction) or it fails to recover planted t on 3/3 toy curves. Feasible single-core <3 min at dim~2000; no timed benchmark on the busy host.
ranked.expected_gain: Large verified constant on the lab's only below-rho validated row and the genus-3 LA-dominated rows. High probability (code exists), low test cost.

ranked.title: Determine the affine-type (2,2,2) codomain type for prime-order genus-3 hyperelliptic Jacobians (quartic vs hyperelliptic): the single gate to a UNIVERSAL 4/3->1 exponent drop
ranked.direction: g3-transfer P1 (cross-genus P2 is the same question, but overclaims it as resolved)
ranked.refutation_attempt: Verified the structural setup by independent exact computation (my lagr.py): exactly 2 F_q-rational Lagrangians for prime order, both affine-type, kernel over F_{q^7} (constant-degree extension), 0 pair-type (so Smith is structurally unavailable, not merely 0 by census - matches smith_near_prime 0/1110). The simplicity chain is sound: #J prime => J F_q-simple => codomain simple => indecomposable dim-3 ppav => a Jacobian (hyperelliptic XOR smooth quartic). Tried to refute the exponent claim: it holds ONLY if the codomain is a quartic, and that is genuinely undetermined - I refuted cross-genus-P2's 'generically a plane quartic': A_3 genericity does NOT transfer to a specific isogeny image, so the honest prior is ~50/50 (g3-transfer's own framing). Second refutation that stands: even a quartic codomain is worthless unless the destination (#1) actually beats q^{4/3} at reachable p; and the determination needs a theta (2,2,2)-isogeny tool + a CAS, neither on host.
ranked.surviving_claim: If the affine (2,2,2) codomain is a plane quartic (decidable on ONE concrete curve by S_8-genericity of the 30 affine Lagrangians), prime-order genus-3 hyperelliptic DLP transfers 4/3->1 on ~100% of curves at poly(log q) transfer cost; the codomain type is the one unresolved binary, and it cannot be settled by combinatorics (even-theta-null vanishing depends on moduli).
ranked.first_test: Cheapest: a literature/KB check first (Smith 2008, Ritzenthaler genus-3 theta criteria) - the affine-quotient type may already be published; research-kb was unavailable to the explorers but should be queried. Then, if still open: compute ONE affine (2,2,2)-isogeny on ONE toy prime-order genus-3 curve over F_{q^7} with a Lubicz-Robert/avisogenies-style tool and read the 36 even theta-nulls. KILL if an even theta-null vanishes (hyperelliptic) on 2-3 independent examples.
ranked.expected_gain: Very high if quartic (universal exponent drop on the cryptographic hyperelliptic class), but gated behind #1 and behind acquiring an isogeny/CAS tool; medium-low probability.

ranked.title: Non-hyperelliptic genus-4 canonical (hyperplane) IC at exponent 4/3 with a CORRECTED instrument - a strictly lower exponent than the lab's best validated (hyperelliptic genus-4, p^1.54)
ranked.direction: nonhyp-diem P2 = cross-genus P3 at g=4
ranked.refutation_attempt: Checked the arithmetic: canonical genus-4 curve has degree 2g-2=6 in P^3, hyperplane through g-1=3 base points leaves residual degree 3, giving e=3 and exponent 2-2/(g-1)=4/3 < hyperelliptic 2LP 3/2 < rho 2 (Oyono-Theriault 2023 / Diem, literature). Tried to kill via the known L08 failure: the only lab attempt is INCONCLUSIVE because duplicate lines were counted as useful relations (111 'useful' vs 0 genuine at p=1031 d=5) and LA was charged before large-prime elimination (d=4 control slope 1.618). So the apparent sub-4/3 slopes are artefacts - the lead is untested, not refuted. Surviving refutations: (i) the margin is only 1/6 (4/3 vs 3/2) and the canonical Pic arithmetic is heavier, so a measured crossover with the hyperelliptic row may sit beyond the reachable p<=54293 (#J 63-bit guard); (ii) it is a DIFFERENT target class from the lab's hyperelliptic genus-4 - a new lower-exponent front, not an improvement to a given instance (no transfer exists, Naranjo-Pirola 2018).
ranked.surviving_claim: A correctly-instrumented (dedup lines once; charge LA after large-prime elimination) non-hyperelliptic genus-4 canonical IC can demonstrate a measurably lower exponent (4/3) than the lab's best validated hyperelliptic genus-4 row on a generic, abundant target class; the d=4 control is the instrument gate.
ranked.first_test: Re-run the L08 d=4 control and the canonical g=4 ladder with the two assessment-mandated fixes on ~5 non-hyperelliptic g=4 curves per prime at p in {1031,4099,16411,54293}. KILL if the d=4 control slope is outside [0.85,1.25] (instrument still broken) or the corrected g=4 total-cost exponent upper-95% >= 1.5. Reuses the L08 grid/curves/FPM model; only the counting rule and LA charge-point change.
ranked.expected_gain: Medium: lower-exponent front vs the best validated row, but small margin and short reachable lever arm. Medium probability, low-medium cost - gated by the d=4 control.

ranked.title: Odd-l (l=3) transfer feasibility census for prime-order genus-3 hyperelliptic (extension-degree k distribution), as a cheap gate before any (3,3,3)-isogeny work
ranked.direction: g3-transfer P3 / cross-genus P2's own falsifying test
ranked.refutation_attempt: The exponent target (4/3->1 on ~25% of prime-order curves per L06 Wilson lower bounds) is the same as #3 but on a smaller fraction and via a DIFFERENT, independent kernel family, so it is a real second shot even if the l=2 affine codomain is hyperelliptic. Refutations that stand: (a) the L06 census is VOID by its own miscalibrated gate (G1 3.75% vs 2% limit), so the ~25% rate is pre-gate; (b) the kernel field degree runs k=13 (l=3) up to 342 (l=7), so the Cantor-over-F_{q^k} plus poly(l^3) theta constant almost certainly exceeds the q^{1/3} head-room over 2LP for l=5,7 - those are dead; (c) codomain type still open (same as #3); (d) dominated by #3 (l=2 gives 100% coverage, F_{q^7}, cheaper). Only l=3 is even worth a feasibility look, and only if a positive-density small-k sub-family exists.
ranked.surviving_claim: Whether a positive-density (say >=5%) sub-family of prime-order genus-3 curves carries a rational l=3 Lagrangian with kernel field degree k<=4 is decidable by a pure-Python charpoly-mod-l census (no CAS, no isogeny) and cleanly gates the entire odd-l route.
ranked.first_test: For prime-order hyperelliptic genus-3 curves over small p, compute the degree-6 Frobenius charpoly (from N1,N2,N3 point counts), reduce mod l in {3,5,7}, enumerate Frobenius-stable Lagrangians of the symplectic (F_l)^6, and record k = order of Frobenius on each kernel. KILL the l=3 route if <5% of prime-order curves have a rational Lagrangian with k<=4. ~1-2 min, pure Python.
ranked.expected_gain: High if a small-k quartic sub-family exists, but low probability (k distribution likely large; codomain open). Cheap test, so worth running alongside #3's literature check.

ranked.title: Orbit-closed triple-large-prime elimination on special-automorphism/RM Jacobians (the only in-lane exponent lever, 2-2/(g-1))
ranked.refutation_attempt: The counting is correct that unstructured t>=3 is strictly WORSE than 2-2/g (confirmed: the 3+-uniform large-prime hypergraph forces ~V'^2=q^{2b} elimination), so the only crack is closed-form orbit dependencies that cheapen elimination to O(V'). Two refutations are close to fatal for the GOAL: (a) prime-order applicability - curves with a rational order->=3 automorphism or computable RM almost always have decomposable or non-prime Jacobians (the exact wall that gave Smith 0/1110), so the method likely never touches a prime-order target; (b) the orbit dependencies may be precisely the L02 constant m-fold factor-base folding in disguise (reduce effective large-prime count by a constant, NOT independent higher-t relations), collapsing the 'exponent lever' to a dead constant. The explorer did not run the decisive orbit-independence test.
ranked.surviving_claim: IF orbit sums supply large-prime dependencies that are rank-independent of factor-base folding AND the special family contains prime-order instances, t=3 could reach 2-2/(g-1); both conjuncts are unlikely for prime-order targets, so this is parked, not pursued.
ranked.first_test: On y^2=x^7+1 over a small p with 7|p-1 (g=3): enumerate degree-1 places, form sigma-orbits, build the large-prime incidence of a few hundred 3-almost-smooth divisors, and check EXACTLY whether its kernel is recovered from orbit sums in O(V') AND is rank-independent of m-fold folding. KILL if not independent (it is the L02 constant) OR if #J is composite for all sampled a (prime-order target unreachable). Pure Python <3 min.
ranked.expected_gain: Speculative exponent lever but near-zero prime-order reach; low probability, parked despite a cheap test.

ranked.title: Genus-2 split/elliptic-subcover obstruction theorem + O((log p)^c) weak-curve detector
ranked.refutation_attempt: I could not refute the mathematics and did not try to - it is correct and I re-derived the core: an isogeny preserves the Frobenius charpoly hence #A=#J, so a split A=E1xE2 forces #J=#E1*#E2 composite; therefore a prime-order genus-2 J is absolutely simple and admits NO (l,l)/Richelot neighbor that is a product and no elliptic subcover. The 660-curve check (0/35 prime-order split; 107/107 split curves composite) is consistent. The refutation is of its STATUS as a breakthrough: it is a negative result (proves there is NO genus-2 exponent route for prime order) plus a hygiene filter that fires on ~0 cryptographic targets - valuable as a guard rail, not an improvement under the success criterion.
ranked.surviving_claim: There is no exponent-moving route for prime-order genus-2 Jacobians over prime fields (genus 2 is the crossover where best IC exponent q^1 = rho q^1); only constants are available, and the lab's measured gap is 3-5x with no crossing. Adopt the detector as cheap cryptographic hygiene and stop seeking a genus-2 exponent.
ranked.first_test: Already done (obstruction.py, 660 curves). No further test needed; optionally fold the detector into the curve-selection pipeline as a negligible-cost filter.
ranked.expected_gain: Zero as an attack; high as a settled obstruction that should redirect all genus-2 effort away from exponent hunts.

Weight-aware purge (la P2): the validated x* matrix is already near-min-weight (SGE(4,1.5) merged only 164/2001 cols and RAISED nnz), and sparse-solver cost may be column-count-bound not weight-bound; headroom likely <10%. KILL any if weight reduction <10% or it does not survive composition with SGE. Pure Python <3 min each. Do not run until #2 is in.
